observations.statement: A component-charge parity Tear gives exact family-specific compression for explicit Tseitin systems, but this relies on access to the correct affine module language.
The equality family E_n has O(n) clauses and 2^n pairwise continuation-distinguishable residuals, terminally refuting a polynomial continuation-complete quotient of all partial-assignment states.
Rich finite structural and signed marginal summaries collide on opposite SAT labels, so such summaries cannot be complete JANUS Tear signatures.
Adding exhaustive unit propagation to the tested marginal signature still permits an exact SAT/UNSAT collision with no unit assignments on either side.
The odd-charge K4 Tseitin contradiction has no width-three Resolution refutation but does have a width-four refutation in the exact finite saturation audit.
A polynomial-size bijective nonlinear re-encoding can preserve an XOR contradiction while destroying visible affinity, so affine-only Tear extraction is representation dependent.
Policy-0A work cannot be represented by unique residual count alone: the K4 fixtures contain thousands of recursive calls, branch edges and incoming memo contexts beyond the cache entries.
MAJ3 is exactly 1-stifling and both output fibres are non-affine, providing the correct gadget interface for the 2026 Resolution-width to Res(⊕)-depth lifting theorem.
Exact residual memoization is a formula-caching inference rather than automatically free ordinary Resolution DAG sharing; the naive Policy-0A-to-Resolution simulation is blocked.
Removing memoization yields Policy-0T, whose MAJ3-lifted K4 run exceeds the explicit 4N^2 recursive-occurrence envelope; the finite result motivates but does not prove the asymptotic H130 route.
